_doc: Graphics quality levels (scripts/world3d/quality.gd): what each costs the phone. The player picks one in Settings; a phone starts on `mid`, a computer on `high`. `scale` is the 3D resolution (the interface stays sharp); `lod_pixels` is how coarse a model may get before a simpler level of it shows (bigger: simpler sooner); `shadow_splits` 1 or 2 (2 is sharper near the camera); `pose_every` is how many frames apart every animal is posed at least (2 on low halves the animals' cost; the farm's own budget, `Animal3D.FULL_RATE`, may space them further when there are many); `crop_shadows` whether crops cast shadows (most of a big farm's shadow triangles); `max_fps` caps the frame rate (0: none, the screen's own rate; a fixed 60 would judder on a 90 Hz screen), so a cheap phone on low runs cooler and longer at an even 30; `screen_grade` keeps the full-screen pass for the low sun's warmth and the vignette (it copies the screen every frame; the rest of the grade is in the 3D frame's own adjustments). `auto`: on a device whose player hasn't chosen yet, the first launch waits `warmup` seconds, then times `frames` frames (skipping any over `max_frame_ms`, a hitch or a resume; leaving the app starts the count again), and keeps one level down when the median frame's work takes more than `down_ms`, or one up when less than `up_ms` (on phones only if `up_on_mobile`: a first farm is the lightest it will ever be, so a phone only steps down; and never up where the renderer can't time itself). Kept once, used from the next launch; the player's choice in Settings always wins.
